entries.officialText:
The number of real roots of the equation \(x^{3} + x - 1 = 0\) is
(A) 0
(B) 1
(C) 2
(D) 3
entries.reasoning: x^3 + x - 1 has derivative 3x^2 + 1 > 0 everywhere, so the function is strictly increasing and crosses the axis exactly once. A cubic always has at least one real root, and monotonicity rules out a second and third.
entries.verification: f'(x) minimum is 1.0 on [-5,5]; bisection gives the single root at x = 0.682327804.

entries.officialText:
Let the quadratic equation \(ax^{2} + bx + c = 0\) have imaginary roots only and the real coefficients \(a, b, c\) obey the relation \(a + b + c < 0\). Then
(A) \(a > 0, c < 0\)
(B) \(a < 0, c > 0\)
(C) \(a > 0, c > 0\)
(D) \(a < 0, c < 0\)
entries.reasoning: Complex roots force a and c to have the same sign, so options A and B are impossible. Since f(1) = a + b + c < 0 and a parabola with a > 0 has a minimum, a > 0 with f(1) < 0 would force real roots; therefore a < 0 and c < 0.
entries.verification: Sign argument on the discriminant and on f(1); no computation is needed once the same-sign condition is used.

(B) \(\log\frac{5}{2}\)

(B) one tangent at origin
(C) two tangents at origin
(D) three tangents at origin

(B) \(\sqrt{3}y - x = a\)
(C) \(\sqrt{3}x + y = \sqrt{3}a\)

entries.reasoning: The normal to a circle at a point passes through the centre, so the normal here is the line through the origin and (a/2, sqrt3 a/2), whose slope is sqrt3: y = sqrt3 x, i.e. sqrt3 x - y = 0.
